sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and script description
sections.what: Describes the script and loads the standard Python tools it needs to read the system, files and paths.
sections.why: Likely reason: the top of the file gathers what the other checks need.

sections.name: print_header
sections.title: Heading printer for each group
sections.what: Prints a boxed title line so each group of checks is easy to find in the output.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the long output readable.

sections.name: print_check
sections.title: Tick or cross line printer
sections.what: Prints a tick or a cross next to a message, depending on whether the check passed.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared function keeps every result line looking the same.

sections.name: check_python_version
sections.title: Checks Python version is 3.9 or newer
sections.what: Reads the installed Python version and reports whether it is 3.9 or newer, which the app needs.
sections.why: Likely reason: older Python versions can fail with newer packages, so this check comes first.
sections.watch_out: The check accepts only major version 3, so a future major version would be marked as failed.

sections.name: check_dependencies
sections.title: Checks that packages can be loaded
sections.what: Tries to load each required package and marks it as installed or missing. It also tries two optional packages, one for PST email files and one for Outlook on Windows, and reports them without affecting the overall result.
sections.why: Likely reason: a missing package is a common cause of the app failing to start.
sections.watch_out: Some package names are converted in a way that does not match the real import names, such as python-dotenv, so correct installs can show as missing.

sections.name: check_env_file
sections.title: Checks the .env settings file
sections.what: Looks for the .env file, loads it, and checks the OpenAI key prefix. Then makes a live call to OpenAI to confirm the key works. Reports SharePoint settings as found or optional.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app cannot call OpenAI without a valid key, so the file is checked early.
sections.watch_out: The result is true whenever the file exists, even when the OpenAI key is rejected, so the summary can show this check as passed.

sections.name: check_tesseract
sections.title: Checks the OCR text reader
sections.what: Tries to load the Python OCR wrapper and read the Tesseract version. Reports whether Tesseract was found, with an install hint if not.
sections.why: Likely reason: reading text from images in PowerPoint files needs Tesseract, so it is checked separately.
sections.watch_out: Any error, including a missing Python package, is reported as Tesseract not found, which can hide the real cause.

sections.name: check_directories
sections.title: Checks the project folders exist
sections.what: Checks that the backend folder and its four subfolders exist. Notes that the data folder will be created on first run. Returns false if a required folder is missing.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app expects this folder layout, so a missing folder points to an incomplete copy.
sections.watch_out: The paths are relative, so the check only works when the script is run from the project folder.

sections.name: check_required_files
sections.title: Checks key program files exist
sections.what: Checks that the main backend file, the config file, the requirements list, the browser page and the Windows start file are present.
sections.why: Likely reason: these files are needed to start the app, so a missing one stops it.
sections.watch_out: The list is typed by hand, so a renamed file must also be updated here.

sections.name: check_port_availability
sections.title: Checks port 8000 is free
sections.what: Tries to connect to port 8000 on this computer. If something answers, reports the port as in use and fails the check. If the check itself errors, it passes with a warning.
sections.why: Likely reason: two programs cannot use the same port, so a busy port blocks the server.
sections.watch_out: A running Universal RAG server answers on port 8000, so this check fails in the normal running state.

sections.name: print_summary
sections.title: Prints the final result
sections.what: Shows either a ready message with next steps, or a list of the checks that failed with a pointer to the setup guide.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the owner one clear place to look after many lines of output.
sections.watch_out: The summary only reflects the results it receives, so a check that wrongly passes will show as ready.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Runs every check and sets the result
sections.what: Runs each check in order, saves each true or false result under a name, prints the summary, and exits with success only if every check passed.
sections.why: Likely reason: collecting every result first means one failure does not hide the others.
sections.watch_out: An uncaught error in any check stops the whole run, so the summary is never printed.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Starts the script when run directly
sections.what: Runs the main function when this file is started directly, and does nothing when another file imports it.
sections.why: Likely reason: this is the usual Python pattern for a file that can be run or imported.

summary: A setup checker that tests the Python version, required packages, the .env settings, the OCR tool, project folders, required files and port 8000, then prints a pass or fail list.
purpose: Tells the owner whether this computer is ready to run Universal RAG before they start the server.
why: Likely reason: setup problems are a common reason the app fails to start, so one check finds them early.
how: It prints a title, then checks the Python version is 3.9 or newer. Next it tries to load each required and optional package. It then loads the .env file and makes a live call to OpenAI to list models. It checks the OCR tool, the project folders and the required files, then checks port 8000 is free. Last, it prints a summary and exits with success only if every check passed.
inputs: The .env file in the current folder, the installed Python packages, the OpenAI key, optional SharePoint settings, the project folder layout, and whether port 8000 is in use.
outputs: Printed tick and cross lines for each check, a summary with the failed checks listed, and an exit code of 0 when everything passed or 1 otherwise.
risks: Several package names are checked with names that do not match the real import names. This includes python-dotenv, python-docx, python-pptx and Pillow, so correct installs can show as missing. The .env check returns true even when the OpenAI key is rejected. The script prints the first 20 characters of the key. A missing dotenv package stops the script with an uncaught error. The port check fails whenever the server is already running.
debug: If a package shows as NOT INSTALLED, check it with pip in the same Python, because the check may be using the wrong import name. If the OpenAI line fails, check the key in .env and the internet connection. If port 8000 is reported in use, check whether the server is already running. Run the script from the project folder, because it looks for files by relative paths.
